travel.transit: You unmake yourself here and remake yourself there. It's fine. It's probably fine.
"You unmake yourself here and remake yourself there. It's fine. It's probably fine. The ferryman's done it a thousand times and only lost the occasional thumb. Step into the circle."

"Passage to {region}? Coin's the same as ever; the risk is yours and it's gone up since the god dropped. New beasts, new hazards, new ways to die. Still want the ticket? Of course you do. You always do."

"The ritual circle takes you apart with great gentleness and reassembles you with most of the original parts in most of the right places. Travel broadens the soul. Sometimes literally. Mind the seams."
tutorial.battle: "The circle closes and only one team walks out whole. AP is your shared pool each turn — basics are cheap, the big rites cost. Focus is per-creature; spend too many heavy moves and it'll exhaust. Don't dawdle: the entropy clock starts when you do."

"Land a status and you change the fight — Petrify a fast thing, Seal a clever one, Wither a wall. Six of them, each named, each a different cruelty. Learn which cruelty fits which problem. That's tactics. That's most of staying alive."

"Your creature can drop without dying — that's a knockout, filed for revival. But push past that and it's gone, truly, a headstone in the Graveyard. Permadeath was always on. It was always on. Fight like you believe me, because I'm right."
tutorial.catch: "Hold out your hand. It'll love you or it'll eat you — sometimes both, in that order. That's how you catch the willing ones. The unwilling ones, we'll cover the trap for. Later. When you're sadder."
"Go on, catch the wounded one. It's mercy and math — easier odds, warmer bond. Most of this craft is mercy and math wearing the same coat."

"The bond does three jobs, child: it lets them grow, it lets you to the Lab-altar, and it lets them disobey a bad order. Earn it slow. A high bond is the most useful thing you'll ever fail to deserve."
tutorial.currency: "Three coins matter here. Drachma ₯ — common coin; the gods don't take it, which tells you everything. Essence ✶ — soul-fuel; every drop was a somebody. Ichor ◈ — divine blood, bottled; spend it like it's the last of someone holy, because it is."

"₯ buys traps and tonics. ✶ fuels the Lab. ◈ buys the things that change you. Notice the pattern: the more a currency costs your soul, the more it can buy your power. There's a whole philosophy in those three glyphs. None of it is comforting."
tutorial.factions: "Two axes draw the world: Order against Chaos, Purity against Corruption. Where you sit on that grid decides which of the nine gods you could become. Every choice nudges your dot. There's no neutral square that lasts. Standing still is also a position. It's just a slow one."

"Court a faction and its rival turns cold — that's the cost, always. The High Table's the one exception: they like you uncommitted. Everyone else wants you to pick. Picking is the game. Refusing to pick is also the game, and a lonelier one."
tutorial.graveyard: "When one dies — truly dies, past a knockout — it goes to the Graveyard, and Goodwife Penne logs it: name, force, how. You can visit. You should. The dead you made are the only ones who'll never lie to you about who you've become."

"The Pale Court will offer to bring your dead back. The offer is real, and so is the interest. Read every term. A clean grief you carry costs less, in the end, than a cheap resurrection you owe. Learn that now, while it's still abstract."
tutorial.husbandry: "There's a fast road and a slow one. The Lab remakes a creature in an afternoon. Breeding takes generations — pair, hatch, select, repeat — chasing a rare gene up out of the blood. Slower. Realer. The Stoneblooded will tell you the slow way is the only way that lasts. They're not entirely wrong."

"Raise a creature gentle and it grows up expecting the world's survivable. Raise it hard and it grows up expecting to be spent. The bond carries your flavor, not just your orders. How you raise it is who you are — and the creature can read that long before you can."
tutorial.lab: "Rule one of the Lab: it's only an abomination if it survives. Rule two: ...oh. That one survived. Congratulations? Drag the method to precise until you've stopped flinching — wild is cheaper and louder and not yet your friend."

"Two creatures go on the table, one comes off. That's a Fuse. Place them, read the cost ledger — the ledger's the only honest thing in here — and when you're sure, seal the rite. After the wax sets, there's no taking it back. There's no taking anything back here. Welcome."

"See the meters? Entropy's the price of pushing too hard. Corruption's the price you can't earn back. Watch both. The bench will let you ignore them. The bench is not your friend either. Nothing in here is. That's why it works."
tutorial.stakes: "The gods are all dead, and we're standing on them. This whole market's on Demeter's elbow. You came to rob a graveyard of powers. Everyone here did. Try to be one of the ones who's honest about it."

"Nine factions will court you, and the moment you take one hand, its rival reaches for a knife. You can't befriend everyone. Pick a hand to become. The factions remember who you snubbed. So does the world. So, eventually, do you."

"Push a creature to a pure force-pole and it ascends — leaves your pocket and becomes a minor god that reshapes your world. That's the spine of everything. Aim a creature at a throne and you aim it away from you. Nobody tells you that part. I just did."

"The Standstill bell means no godhood inside the walls. Ascend in the city and the Watch escorts you out to finish like everyone else. It's the one rule Threshold keeps. It keeps it because a market can't run with a fresh god in the foyer. Reasonable, really. Most horrors are."
tutorial.welcome: "Welcome to Threshold — the last mortal city, and very proud of the 'last.' You begin a nobody with an old knack. The city has a betting pool on how far you get. Let's surprise it."
"First rule of the craft: a creature you catch can love you; a creature you build owes you. Neither is safe. Pick one anyway — that's the whole game in a sentence."
"You've got the old knack. Lucky you. The last three I taught it to are dead, dead, and a minor god of drainage. Mixed results. Pay attention and aim for 'god of something nicer.'"

ui.tooltip.bond: How much this creature trusts you not to put it on the table.
ui.tooltip.corruption: What you spend that you can't earn back. Opens doors. Bolts others shut forever.
ui.tooltip.drachma: Coin. The gods don't take it, which tells you everything.
ui.tooltip.entropy: The price of pushing too hard, too fast. It does not refund.
ui.tooltip.essence: Soul-fuel. Every drop was a somebody.
ui.tooltip.focus: Composure under the knife. Runs out faster than you'd like.
ui.tooltip.ichor: Divine blood, bottled. Spend it like it's the last of someone holy. It is.
ui.tooltip.luck: The thumb the cosmos keeps on the scale. Whose, it won't say.
ui.tooltip.purity: How close this one is to becoming a god and leaving you behind.
weather.dawn: Dawn, such as it is. The world survived another rotation, which it manages mostly out of habit now.
First light finds you still here, still climbing. The cosmos files this under persistent. It's not a compliment. It's not not one.
The dark lifts off {region} like a debt deferred, not paid. Morning's just the interest break. Use it.
A new day. The Graveyard didn't grow overnight, which is either your doing or your luck. Don't ask which. Don't make it answer.
weather.dusk: The light goes. In a graveyard of gods, the dark is just the part where you can hear them better.
Dusk. The lamplighter starts his rounds — keeps the dark organized. Won't stop a god. Stops the smaller things. The smaller things are most of what gets you.
Night falls over {region}. The day-beasts bed down; the other kind wake and go looking. Mind which kind you are.
Last light. Whatever you were going to finish today, the day has stopped waiting for you to finish it.
weather.force: A Gaia-pressure front rolls in — the air goes heavy, the ground attentive. Bulk-blooded things wake. The rest of you should sit down.
An Ouranos squall tears through. Everything light moves twice; everything slow moves once and regrets it.
A Cosmos calm settles over the land — too even, too quiet, the weather of a place that has filed away its surprises.
A Chaos-cell forms, and the sky forgets which way down is. Briefly. Enjoyably. Catastrophically.
An Eros bloom-front passes through and the dead grass tries, hopefully, to grow. Some of it succeeds. Some of it shouldn't have.
A Thanatos chill comes down like a held breath let out slow. Nothing dies that wasn't going to. It just dies sooner, and tidier.
weather.rare: "Something rare in the sky tonight — a conjunction the oracles charge double to misread. The fauna's restless. The veil's thin. On nights like this, things get caught that usually can't be. Hunt accordingly."

"The entropy-tide crests higher than it has in an age. Every meter that can climb is climbing past its marks. The old hands call this a 'making night' — when legends and abominations both come cheap, and the difference between them is a coin-flip and a flinch."
"A still moment — no weather, no tide, no wind, nothing moving anywhere. The world holding its breath. It does this, rarely, and no one knows for what. Enjoy the quiet. Distrust it. Both."
weather.shift: "The force-weather's turning. What favored you an hour ago is about to favor the other side. Read the sky; the sky is a battlefield bias with no loyalty."
"A front rolls in off the dead god's domain — the climate here always carries the flavor of whatever fell. Spawns shift, gene-expression bends, advantage tilts. Adjust, or be adjusted."
"Storm warning, of a sort: the entropy and the weather are climbing together, and when they crest at once the region gets strange. The locals board up. The Revel throws a party. Pick which you are."
weather.tide: The entropy-tide is rising. The world's instability climbs with it — push hard now and the bench will push back harder.
Low tide. The entropy settles, the routes that were sealed grind open, and the patient get their hour. Spend it.
High entropy-tide — the slag thaws, the warps deepen, and everything volatile gets more so. The Sunder is delighted. You should be careful.
The tide turns. Somewhere a tide-locked door opens; somewhere another seals behind it. The world breathes. You're inside the lung.
Entropy crests. Every meter that can climb is climbing. This is when legends get made and creatures get unmade, often in the same heartbeat.
weather.tide_locked: "The tide's low — a route that was sealed grinds open. It won't stay. Through it now, or wait a cycle and gamble the patience. The world doesn't hold doors."
"High tide seals the slag-crossing. The molten flow's back, the path's gone, and it'll be gone until the cycle turns. Forgefell keeps its own clock and shares it with no one."
"A tide-timed gate. The world breathes, and on the exhale this door is shut. Time your crossing to the lung, not your impatience. The lung wins every argument."
